Our legal is pushing for a 30-day notice to opt out of auto-renew and a 30-day TFC window for pilots. Can Redwood accommodate 30/30 (30-day auto-renew notice + 30-day TFC)? From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — term and renewal

Tom — thanks for the note and the Order Form. Short answer: we can be flexible for pilots but need to balance economics and operational predictability for production commitments. High-level proposal below; happy to adjust with procurement/legal input.

Proposed compromise (for the Order Form/pilot you shared):
- Initial term: 6 months (pilot) or 12 months (production) — choose per the Order Form line item.
- Auto-renew: renews for the same term length unless either party provides written notice prior to 60 days before the end of the then-current term.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): mutual TFC permitted with 60 days written notice; if the customer terminates during the initial 3 months of a 12-month contract, a pro-rata early termination amount equal to unused prepaid fees will apply (we can cap for pilots).

Rationale: 60-day notice aligns with our capacity planning and allows us to offboard caches and reserved capacity without service disruption. For pilots we can accept shorter notice if Acme commits a small non-refundable onboarding fee.

If that sounds reasonable I will loop in Legal (Mina) and Ben on pricing carveouts and get a redline today.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Mina / Ben — forwarding Acme's ask. Summary and asks below.

Summary: Acme wants 30-day auto-renew notice + 30-day TFC. We prefer 60-day for both (see my note to Tom) but are open to a hybrid.

Asks: 
1) Mina — please review the MSA and Order Form redlines with focus on auto-renew language, notice window, and TFC economics. Two options to consider in the redline: (A) mutual 45-day notice (middle ground), or (B) 60-day for production / 30-day for pilots with onboarding fee. Please mark any required concessions (credits, pro-rata refund language, early termination fees) and include fallback wording for operational handoff obligations. Need by EOD 10/11 to keep procurement cadence.
2) Ben — confirm whether pricing adjustments (onboarding fee or early termination cap) are OK to offer for the pilot; if so, propose numbers and I'll present.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v2.docx (attached).

Thanks — Jasmine

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form questions — term and renewal (Acme) — legal redline request

Jasmine / Ben — thanks for the context. Attached is a marked-up redline (Redlines_Acme_OrderForm_legal_v1.docx). High-level recommendations: 

1) Auto-renew: change to 45-day written notice prior to term end (compromise position). 
2) TFC (mutual): allow mutual termination for convenience with 45 days' written notice. For 12-month production terms, include pro-rata refund for prepayments and require 30 days to wind down active deployments to avoid abrupt service loss; propose a service handoff schedule to be included as an Order Form appendix. 
3) Pilot carve-out: for pilot Order Forms <= 6 months, permit 30-day notice and TFC if Acme agrees to a one-time non-refundable onboarding fee equal to one month of committed spend.
4) Operational obligations: require written offboarding plan and cooperation clause; exclude cached data retention beyond 30 days unless a separate data-retention fee is agreed.

If Ben confirms the onboarding fee and whether we can waive the pro-rata cap for pilots, we can send the redline to Acme. I flagged fallback language for disputes and added an explicit 'no implied renewal' clause.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Tom — thanks for the patience. We've consolidated internal feedback and propose the following for Acme's Order Form: 

- Initial term: Pilot: 6 months (as requested). Production: 12 months if converted.
- Auto-renew: 45-day written notice prior to the end of the then-current term (compromise).
- TFC: mutual termination for convenience with 45 days' written notice. For pilots (<=6 months) Redwood will accept 30-day notice if Acme agrees to a one-time non-refundable onboarding fee equal to one month of committed spend.
- Refunds/fees: pro-rata refunds for prepaid fees on termination; onboarding fee credited toward first 3 months for conversions to production.
- Operational handoff: include a 30-day cache/data retention default and a short offboarding plan appendix (we can draft).

Attached is the redline from our legal team. If Acme is comfortable with the 45/45 compromise (or the pilot 30/one-month-fee option), I can circulate a DocuSign link and a clean Order Form for signature.
